# All Shropshire Mobility: All Shropshire Mobility is a vehicle adaptations company based near Shrewsbury in Shropshire. We started our business over fifteen years ago, and during that time we have built good working relationships with all the major car adaptation companies, enabling us to offer a bespoke service with a fantastic back-up.

- [Taking A Practical Driving Test With A Disability](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/taking-a-practical-driving-test-with-a-disability/): If you have a disability, you will still need to take the same driving test accessed by non-disabled drivers. UK law requires that all drivers must be able to drive safely on the road in different traffic conditions and are also expected to know the highway code. This must be demonstrated during the test - it is no easier for people with a disability, the result will still be a pass or fail.
- [Motability: What To Do If You&#8217;re In A Car Accident](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/motability-what-to-do-if-youre-in-a-car-accident/): Car accidents are extremely common but also unexpected – an occurrence which takes place in a matter of seconds but can have drastic repercussions. A car accident is upsetting and inconvenient at the least and life-changing at the worst. In such a situation it can be difficult to know what to do, as events happen so rapidly that the details of the accident itself, can seem somewhat of a blur. However, there are several steps which can be taken to prevent a bad situation from getting worse, as well as ensuring your insurance is paid out.
- [Vehicle Adaptations for Upper Body Disabilities](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/vehicle-adaptations-upper-body-drivers/): Driving aids and adaptations are suitable for those with both lower and upper body disabilities or weaknesses. The following adaptations may be helpful for those with upper body disabilities.
- [Who Can Qualify for Motability?](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/who-can-qualify-for-motability/): The Motability scheme refers to a UK charity organisation which allows disabled people to lease a car, scooter, powered wheelchair or other types of wheelchair accessible vehicle. The scheme was founded by Lord Sterling of Plaistow in 1977 and has helped to provide thousands of people with disabilities access to their own vehicle, which in turns brings with it, greater flexibility and freedom. This allows individuals who might otherwise struggle, to visit friends and relatives, go to work, do the shopping and so forth.
- [How In-Car Technology Can Help Drivers With Disabilities](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/how-in-car-technology-can-help-drivers-with-disabilities/): Built-in car technology has advanced considerably over the past decade, many of these developments can facilitate the lives of all drivers, including those with disabilities.
- [Driving With Diabetes](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-with-diabetes/): Most people with diabetes are able to hold a full driving license and carry on driving – there are however a number of ways in which diabetes can potentially impair driving, this can depend on the medication used to treat your type of diabetes, how controlled it is and whether or not you have any other health conditions which may affect your ability to drive.
- [Driving Following A Brain Injury](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-following-a-brain-injury/): Housed inside the hard protective casing of the skull, the brain itself is a soft tissue structure which can be damaged as a result of a severe impact to the skull.  A brain injury can occur as a result of accident, such as a fall, during contact sports, or it may be the result of deliberate trauma.
- [Changes To The Blue Badge Scheme &#8211; August 2019](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/changes-to-the-blue-badge-scheme-august-2019/): The Blue Badge scheme is a government initiative designed to help those with severe mobility issues, allowing them to them park as close as possible to their desired destination. The scheme was originally implemented in the 1970s, however new changes have been introduced to widen the Blue Badge eligibility criteria, to include those with hidden disabilities such as autism. These changes are set to roll out in August 2019 and are the biggest overhaul to the system in over 40 years.
- [Driving With Cerebral Palsy](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-with-cerebral-palsy/): Cerebral Palsy (CP) is the name given to a group of life long neurological conditions which can affect muscle control, coordination, reflexes, posture and balance. CP typically develops before, during or shortly after birth – symptoms may not be immediately noticeable and often only become apparent during the first 2-3 years of the child’s life.
- [What To Look For When Shopping For Wheelchair Accessible Cars](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/shopping-for-wheelchair-accessible-cars/): If you will be driving the vehicle yourself, it is probably a good idea to focus on looking for wheelchair accessible cars, although wheelchair accessible vans undeniably offer a wide range of benefits and are usually the preferred option for those being driven rather than driving themselves. Vans however, tend to require more space – not only due to the sheer size of the vehicle, but also for the space required to use the ramp/lift.
- [Driving After A Stroke](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-after-a-stroke/): A stroke is a serious, often life-threatening illness which occurs when parts of the blood supply to the brain are cut off. The sooner the individual receives treatment for the stroke, the less likely it is for permanent damage to occur. Most strokes occur as a result of a blood clot, although in some cases a stroke may occur due to haemorrhage – caused by bleeding in or around the brain. Transient Ischaemic Attack (TIA) is a related condition, it is frequently described as a mini stroke where the blood supply to the brain is temporarily interrupted. This may last for a few minutes, or persist for up to 24 hours, in some cases it may serve as a warning that a full stroke is imminent. Strokes affect people in different ways, some people are left with serious problems caused by the injury to their brain.
- [Driving With Multiple Sclerosis (MS)](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-with-multiple-sclerosis-ms/): Following a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) it is common for individuals to worry about how the condition may potentially impact their day to day life – a key concern is their ability to drive. Driving a car for many is the key to freedom and independence, therefore one of the most common questions asked following a diagnosis of MS is ‘Will I still be able to drive?’ Most people will be able to continue driving. Although driving is a complex activity which can be affected by MS, there are therefore some important considerations to bear in mind. MS can also change over time, resulting in difficulty controlling a vehicle – it is however, important to remember that many people with MS remain happy and confident drivers.
- [Driving After An Amputation](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/driving-after-an-amputation/): Following any type of amputation, the DVLA must be contacted. This is true regardless of the type of amputation, however small. Non-disclosure can result in a fine of up to £1000 if the DVLA is not informed about any condition which may affect your driving.
- [How To Apply For A Blue Badge](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/how-to-apply-for-a-blue-badge/): The blue badge is allocated to the holder rather than any one particular vehicle – this includes taxis and hire cars. Applicants don’t need to be able to drive to apply for a blue badge.
- [Adapting Sports Cars For Disabled Drivers](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/adapting-sports-cars-for-disabled-drivers/): It is a surprisingly common misconception that disabled drivers don’t usually drive luxury or sports cars. Vehicle adaptations however, can be fitted to a wide range of cars, including sports cars and luxury model vehicles making this possible, as well as assuring that drivers with a disability have access to a wide variety of different vehicles, and are able to enjoy a dream car.
- [Proud Sponsors of Shropshire Wheelchair Tennis Tournament](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/proud-sponsors-of-shropshire-wheelchair-tennis-tournament/): All Shropshire Mobility were the proud sponsors of Shropshire Wheelchair Tennis at the annual tennis tournament awarded by the Tennis Foundation/ LTA. The tournament, held at the Shrewsbury Club every August, is now in its ninth successive year.
- [Personal Independence Payment (PIP) and Motability](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/personal-independence-payment-pip-and-motability/): Personal Independence Payment (PIP) is a type of benefit set to gradually replace Disability Living Allowance (DLA). First introduced back in 1992, DLA was designed to assist both adults and children with personal care or mobility needs. PIP is part of the government’s 2013 welfare reform which states its aim is to make the benefit system fairer, and to help those with disabilities lead full and independent lives.
- [Celebrating 40 Years of Motability](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/celebrating-40-years-of-motability/): On the 25th April 2017, the 40th anniversary of Motability was commemorated by an exceptional celebration hosted by Her Majesty The Queen, at Windsor Castle – the world famous Royal residence in Windsor.
- [Motability Insurance &#8211; What You Need To Know](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/motability-insurance-what-you-need-to-know/): The Motability scheme enables those entitled to disability allowance to use their payment to lease a car, scooter or powered wheelchair. This charity organisation has helped millions of people across the UK to become mobile.
- [What Is Motability and How Can You Benefit?](https://www.allshropshiremobility.co.uk/blog/what-is-motability-and-how-can-you-benefit/): The Motability scheme was established in the 1970s and is a charity organisation designed to help disabled individuals remain mobile. It allows those who qualify for certain types of disability allowance to exchange their weekly payment to cover the cost of leasing a new car, scooter or wheelchair accessible vehicle (WAV).
